newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says Erbakan to visit Germany this year.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says Erbakan to visit Germany this year.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday that Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan would visit Germany this year but the date had not yet been set.
At a news conference, Kohl declined to answer a journalist's question about how he viewed Erbakan's pro-Islamic government.
But he pointed out he supported President Suleyman Demirel's policy of maintaining the secular traditions of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk, the founder of modern Turkey.
"I like that a lot. If you want my opinion, all those who stray from this path do not appeal to me," he said.

Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel expressed concern on Tuesday that Turkey was turning towards closer ties with its Moslem neighbours out of deep disappointment with the European Union's failure to help it.
"Turkey feels that it is wrongly treated by Europe," he told journalists.

Turkey has complained bitterly to the EU that it has received no benefits from a new customs union with Brussels because Greece has blocked any bid to give it funds linked to the trade deal, he added.
Washington and its European allies plan meetings in the next few days to assess the risks of a major new crisis between Greece and Turkey over the divided island of Cyprus.

They say Turkey -- an important ally for the West because it borders volatile regions of the Caucasus and the Middle East -- could block NATO decisions in retaliation, including the alliance's planned enlargement to Eastern Europe.
Kinkel also said Islam would become an increasingly important factor in the foreign policy of Moslem countries.
"There is resentment in the Islamic world," he said.
